# Results — Study 423 (Force Index) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Elder's 13-day
Force Index `EMA13((Cₜ−Cₜ₋₁)·Vₜ)`, turned into a long/flat (and long/short) timing rule:
**long while FI(13) > 0, flat while ≤ 0**, entered with one execution lag, and raced **NET**
of one-way costs × NAV against **buy-and-hold**, excess-of-cash to excess-of-cash. As-of
**2026-06-23** (the partial 2026-06-24 bar is dropped). Close is Yahoo total-return-adjusted
(splits + dividends).*

## The honest test — FI(13) long/flat vs buy-and-hold, NET 1 bp one-way

The fair way to judge a part-time-in-cash timing rule is an **excess-vs-excess Sharpe
race** with a HAC *t* on the *daily return difference* (strategy − buy-and-hold).

| Ticker | n (days) | flips/yr | FI Sharpe | Buy-hold Sharpe | mean diff (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** | 8405 | 18.0 | **0.30** | **0.64** | **−3.450** | **−4.03** |
| QQQ | 6863 | 19.1 | 0.24 | 0.52 | −3.995 | −2.98 |
| DIA | 7149 | 17.9 | 0.33 | 0.56 | −2.734 | −2.90 |
| IWM | 6555 | 19.3 | 0.15 | 0.47 | −3.595 | −2.74 |
| XLE | 6915 | 18.0 | 0.20 | 0.43 | −3.537 | −2.21 |
| GLD | 5430 | 15.0 | 0.64 | 0.64 | −1.395 | −1.31 |

- The Force-Index timing rule **underperforms buy-and-hold on every tape**, significantly
  so (HAC *t* < −2) on five of six. On SPY it earns Sharpe **0.30** vs buy-and-hold's
  **0.64** — a **−3.45 bps/day** drag at HAC *t* = **−4.03**.
- In annualised terms SPY FI(13) returns **+3.27%/yr** vs buy-and-hold's **+11.97%/yr**.
- The rule is in the market only **58.4%** of the days; its zero-crosses pull it out of
  the market during the up-legs that generate the equity premium.

## FI period sweep (SPY, long/flat, NET 1 bp)

| FI window | flips/yr | FI Sharpe | HAC *t* (diff vs buy-hold) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| FI(2) — Elder's short-term trigger | 45.8 | 0.17 | **−5.32** |
| FI(13) — Elder's trend filter | 18.0 | 0.30 | **−4.03** |
| FI(50) | 9.3 | 0.36 | **−3.62** |

No FI window rescues it; the fast FI(2) churns hardest and is worst.

## vs the simpler benchmarks (SPY, long/flat, NET 1 bp)

If the price×volume idea added information, FI should beat a plain trend/momentum filter.

| Rule | Sharpe | mean diff vs buy-hold (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Force Index(13) | 0.30 | −3.450 | −4.03 |
| **SMA 50/200** | **0.74** | −0.722 | −0.97 |
| RSI(14) > 50 | 0.44 | −2.813 | −3.31 |
| Buy & hold | 0.64 | — | — |

The plain **SMA(50/200)** filter *beats* buy-and-hold (0.74 vs 0.64; its diff is not
significantly negative) — a real, modest trend effect. Force Index, with its extra volume
term, is the **worst** rule of the four. The volume multiplication subtracts value.

## Cost sweep (SPY FI(13) long/flat)

| One-way cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* (diff) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bp (gross) | 0.34 | −3.87 |
| 1.0 bp | 0.30 | −4.03 |
| 2.0 bp | 0.27 | −4.18 |
| 5.0 bp | 0.17 | −4.66 |

The rule is behind buy-and-hold (0.64) **even gross**; there is no positive break-even
cost — costs only widen the gap.

## Long/short FI(13) (SPY, NET 1 bp, borrow 50 bp/yr)

| Variant | net Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | mean diff (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| FI(13) long/short | **−0.30** | 0.64 | −6.983 | **−4.08** |

Shorting on the down-cross makes it outright **negative** — the down-crosses do not flag
declines, they flag up-legs you then short.

## Sign-permutation placebo (SPY FI(13) long/flat, 1 bp, 1000 draws)

Shuffle the position vector (preserve the exposure profile, destroy the timing alignment):

| Real Sharpe gap vs buy-hold | one-sided *p* (shuffle gap ≥ real) |
|---|--:|
| **−0.341** | **0.824** |

The real gap is on the wrong side of zero and **no better than a shuffle** (~82% of
shuffles beat it) — there is no genuine timing skill in the zero-cross beyond its exposure.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) where yesterday's **signed
dollar-volume flow** genuinely predicts tomorrow's return, the *same* FI(13) long/short
engine recovers the edge and beats buy-and-hold, scaling with the planted strength:

| Planted edge | FI net Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | HAC *t* (diff) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.31 | +0.18 | −1.33 |
| 0.10 | +0.20 | +0.20 | +0.01 |
| 0.20 | +0.72 | +0.22 | +1.25 |
| 0.40 | +1.77 | +0.24 | **+3.46** |
| 0.70 | +2.92 | +0.09 | **+5.49** |

Permutation *p*: **0.735** at the null (no edge), **0.002** at planted = 0.40 (real edge
detected). The engine is a faithful detector — so the real-tape verdict is a statement about
the **market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** FI(13) long/flat NET Sharpe **0.30** vs buy-and-hold **0.64** on SPY;
  daily diff **−3.45 bps**, HAC *t* = **−4.03**; negative on all six tapes; sign-permutation
  *p* = **0.82**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Behind buy-and-hold even gross (Sharpe 0.34); long/short is
  *negative* (−0.30); no positive break-even cost exists.
- **Flags reversals? — BUSTED.** A plain SMA(50/200) filter beats both Force Index *and*
  buy-and-hold; the price×volume twist adds churn, not foresight.
